newsitem.title: UK: Zinc physical premiums pick up, UK copper off high.
newsitem.headline: Zinc physical premiums pick up, UK copper off high.

text.p: Premiums for good quality physical zinc in Europe are firming steadily, while copper premiums have eased from recent highs, physical traders said on Friday.
A mixture of dwindling LME stocks and higher cash prices was helping to boost zinc premiums.
"Everyone was waiting for prices to go down and used up their own stocks. But now they don't have any stocks left, so demand is up," one trader said.
Special high grade zinc out of Rotterdam was being quoted at a spot premium of $30/$40 over LME cash or even $5 firmer for the best grades, compared to $25/$30 earlier in the month.
Another trader said Europe "isn't booming, but consuming well".

"LME stocks are decreasing regularly, there's a shortage of concentrate in the market and the galvanising sector in Europe is buoyant. All this is genuinely bringing about a better price," the trader said.
But premiums for CIS material were unchanged.
Meanwhile in copper, premiums in Northern Europe had eased back after topping out at around $50/$60 earlier this month.
"Consumers are not buying at those numbers anymore. Premiums have definitely eased back," a trader said, citing $40/$50.
Some traders said business in Europe was ticking over in decent quantities, particularly in Germany.
"Business is quite good without being fantastic in the UK, although it's not so great in Italy and France," one said.
But others said business was slower than might be expected ahead of the summer lull.
"They should be stocking up now. But the cash price is too high and people are waiting until it comes off," a trader said.
